answer: Because the forge index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the echo audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 35 aliases hence needs 35 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a spiral index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
